body:
priya: Heads-up — starting ~10:10 UTC we saw a spike of TLS handshake failures at the edge for services that require mTLS. Error: "alert(SSL/TLS): handshake failure" in envoy logs. Not all regions, mostly ap-southeast-1 and us-west-2.
kevin: :rotating_light: saw similar. Do we think this is certchain order or KMS unwrap?
maria: My initial grep shows 502 with downstream TLS errors like `tls: unknown certificate` and `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` from the proxy side.
andrew: Any recent RBAC changes on the KMS keys used for decrypting private keys? I merged the key-access policy PR yesterday but scoped service principal differently.
priya: @andrew yes — we tightened KMS decrypt permissions for the cert-decryption role to the new regional principals. Maybe we missed a regional alias.
kevin: Can we get snippet from envoy where handshake fails? Here's one from edge-1 (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-18T10:12:01Z] envoy error] tls error: TLS handshake error from 10.12.8.44:34218: remote error: handshake failure
[2026-03-18T10:12:01Z] envoy debug] ssl_proceed: cert verify failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```
maria: Also seeing this pattern in cloudwatch for ap-southeast-1: multiple pods failing to mount `tls-secret` because secret decryption failed: `kms:DecryptionDenied`.
andrew: That points at KMS. Which key alias are the secrets using? `alias/redwood/tls/edge/ap-southeast-1` ?
priya: Correct. Our cert-manager pipeline stores encrypted PKCS12 blobs in k8s secrets, wrapped with KMS keys per-region. The decrypt happens during sidecar startup via the secret-syncer.
kevin: If decrypt denied, secret-syncer falls back to reading plaintext from cached volume only if present. Looks like cache miss in those pods. So handshake -> no cert -> handshake failure.
sre-bot: Incident bot: opened INC-2026-013 cert-decrypt-failures. Pager duty: eng-oncall + eng-security.
maria: Quick triage: check KMS condition history in CloudTrail for Decrypt on the regional key. Also confirm the IAM principal for secret-syncer still matches new principal name.
andrew: I checked CloudTrail: Decrypt calls from secret-syncer principal are returning AccessDenied starting at 10:09 UTC. RequestParameters show keyId arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:123456789:key/abcd-efgh. Principal was `service-account:secret-syncer@ap-southeast-1` — the new RBAC policy expects `service-account:secret-syncer@ap-southeast-1-v2`. So mismatch.
priya: That explains it. But why only some pods? Because some nodes were still running the v2 serviceaccount (canary) and others already rolled to the old name. We need a rollout-safe mitigation.
kevin: Mitigation options: 1) revert the RBAC change on KMS to allow both principals for 30m, 2) update secret-syncer on remaining nodes to v2 SA via daemonset restart, 3) unseal cached secrets on affected nodes manually. Fastest is option 1.
maria: I agree revert for safety. I'll open the KMS policy rollback and add both principals temporarily.
andrew: Add audit hooks: when we change key policies, post to #eng-security and trigger a dry-run against CloudTrail to surface impacted principals.
priya: Agreed. Also we need to check long term: rotate to using short-lived signing keys with an identity service token so we don't have per-SA KMS bindings.
kevin: Forensics note: we also saw a downstream error where some clients failed on SNI mismatch after the restart. Looks like a small set of clients had cached old SNI pins — I think due to TLS session resumption with expired cert. Might be unrelated but flagging for vuln triage.
maria: On ciphers: while digging logs I saw `TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA` in a handful of older mobile clients. We should list them for a planned hardening — but not during this incident rollback.
priya: Action items: (1) maria to rollback KMS policy to allow both SA names for 45m (actioned), (2) andrew to push a coordinated daemonset restart of secret-syncer canary -> v2, (3) kevin to verify envoy cert reload paths won't drop connections during secret re-attach, (4) I will open a postmortem and add RBAC checklist.
maria: Done — I pushed a policy change that adds the old SA ARN back. CloudTrail now shows Decrypt success at 10:22 UTC.
sre-bot: Auto: INC-2026-013 status updated -> mitigation in place. Monitoring: decrypt errors down to baseline.
andrew: Rolling restart scheduled at 10:40 UTC in ap-southeast-1 to move remaining pods to v2 SA. Will coordinate with oncall.
kevin: Post-restore validation: run `openssl s_client -connect edge-public:443 -servername svc.example --tls1_2` from three regions + confirm successful handshake and correct cert chain. Add this as step in deploy playbook.
priya: Also need KMS audit logging improvements: ensure we capture `principalIdentity` fields and map to k8s SA names in our CloudTrail-to-ELK parser. Right now they come back as opaque ARN fragments.
maria: For longer term: consider moving private keys into HSM-backed PKCS#11 provider used by the runtime process instead of decrypting at container startup. That removes the secret-syncer KMS margin. But engineering effort.
kevin: Agreed, make a RFC. For now I'll update the KB with quick triage steps and add a snippet for `kubectl` to check decrypt errors: 
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --query "Events[?contains(CloudTrailEvent, 'secret-syncer')].{time:EventTime,arn:Username,err:ErrorMessage}" --region ap-southeast-1
```
priya: Thanks team. Keeping this thread as the incident notes. I'll draft the postmortem and include: timeline, root cause (RBAC principal rename mismatch), mitigation, and follow-ups (policy dry-run, HSM exploration, cipher hardening backlog).
certs-bot: Reminder: upcoming cert rotation for edge CA in 6 days. Ensure postmortem actions are tracked before rotation window.
kevin: :thumbsup: Closing loop — will add tickets and assign owners in the incident doc.
priya: Closing here, will ping when postmortem is published. Thanks!"
